s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neck pain with radiating symptoms to the left hand and associated neurological deficits
salient_findings: Electrical pain radiating to the left hand
Weakness in fine movements and weak grip of the left hand
Atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand
key_facts: 6-month history of progressive neck pain
Pain radiates to the left hand
Numbness in the C8–T1 dermatomes
Weakness in fine movements of the left hand
Weak grip of the left hand
Atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand
Motor testing of the left hand revealed muscle strength of 3/5
Marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra on CT
Lesion involves the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments
Lesion does not significantly compromise the thecal sac

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of progressive neck pain with radiating symptoms and osteolytic lesion on imaging

shortlist.label: Osteolytic metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of osteolytic lesions and could explain neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Known to cause osteolytic lesions and could lead to spinal cord compression

shortlist.label: Plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain osteolytic lesion and associated neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic disease that could cause osteolytic lesions and neurological deficits

raw.rationale: The presence of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, along with the involvement of the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments and the absence of significant compromise to the thecal sac, are consistent with the characteristics of a giant cell tumor, which is known for its aggressive bone destruction and potential to extend into surrounding soft tissues.

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Chordomas typically show high signal intensity on T2-weighted MRI images, which is not described in the case.

rejected.label: Osteolytic metastasis
rejected.why: While osteolytic metastases can cause significant bone destruction, the specific pattern of involvement and the lack of other metastatic sites make this less likely.

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Plasmacytomas are typically associated with multiple myeloma and would more likely present with systemic symptoms and other bone lesions.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
rejected.why: Similar to plasmacytoma, multiple myeloma would likely present with systemic symptoms, other bone lesions, and specific laboratory findings not mentioned in the case.
